title: Kill switch and 15:45 force-close only close positions in the in-memory open_spreads dict — restart or crash leaves live positions that neither the kill switch nor the EOD flatten can ever close
reason: Reproduced from code. open_spreads is a plain dict (position.py:33) with no persistence anywhere in the package (grep for json.dump/save/load/sqlite/pickle: none). reconcile() (position.py:85-100) only computes a report dict and writes an audit line — it never adopts positions into open_spreads and never closes anything. kill_switch_close_all() (position.py:102-111) and the EOD path (main.py:131-1
fix: Make broker state the enforcement source: (1) In reconcile(), classify option positions via asset_class=='us_option' (fallback: OCC type char at symbol[-9]), group untracked legs into spreads (same underlier+expiry, opposite sides, equal |qty|) and adopt each into open_spreads under a synthetic tag with qty from the broker position (abs), status='adopted'; lone legs (Alpaca closed only the short leg) are adopted as single-leg entries closed via close_position. For adopted spreads set the close debit cap to parity (width*100 from OCC strikes), NOT entry_credit*10, since entry credit is unknown. (2) Rewrite kill_switch_close_all() to fetch get_all_positions and close every option position — matched tags via their stored SpreadCandidate reverse mleg, unmatched/adopted ones via reverse mleg built from the position symbols (ratio_qty '1', position_intent buy_to_close/sell_to_close per current side, qty = strategy units, positive debit limit_price, fresh client_order_id each attempt since mleg replace is 403-disabled) — closing spreads ONLY via reverse mleg, never close_position, per platform facts. (3) Persist open_spreads to a JSON file under audit_dir on every register/pop/adopt and reload at boot as a secondary net. (4) Cancel working veritas-open-* orders before closing (see finding 3) and alert loudly (audit + stdout) whenever broker option positions != internal state.

title: No intra-day risk management executes at all: profit-take, 200% stop, and 0DTE 15:30 force-close are dead code, and the daily-loss kill switch is only evaluated in cycles where the LLM proposal passes validation — daily loss can reach ~2x the $2k limit
reason: Reproduced: grep for '.manage(' across the repo returns zero call sites — profit-take, 200% stop, and the 15:30 0DTE force-close (position.py:50-83, config.py:71/75-76) are dead code. main.py:66-67 returns when 'not report.passed or report.corrected is None', and validate() returns corrected=None for NO_TRADE (validator.py:21), so evaluate() and the kill gate (main.py:71-75) execute only in cycles
fix: (1) Call await pm.manage(marks) once per run_cycle and inside reconcile_loop, building mark_prices via get_option_latest_quote on both legs (conservative close-cost mark = short-leg ask minus long-leg bid, given 15-min-delayed indicative data). (2) Hoist account protection out of the proposal path: at the top of run_cycle (after snapshot, before brain.decide) and inside reconcile_loop, fetch the account, compute pnl_today, and if pnl_today <= -SETTINGS.max_daily_loss immediately cancel all open veritas orders (get_orders then cancel_order_by_id) and call kill_switch_close_all — never gate this on LLM output or validation. Optionally also block new submissions when loss is beyond the kill level. (3) Keep kill_switch_close_all's return value and retry failed closes (see finding 7 fix).

title: Position-count and portfolio-heat gates ignore accepted-but-unfilled orders — consecutive cycles can each pass the gates and leave more spreads working/filled than the <=4-position and <=8%-heat limits allow
reason: Reproduced. risk.py:62-69 computes position_count and heat exclusively from snap.positions, which data.py:75-77 fills from get_all_positions (filled positions only). open_credit_spread (broker.py:104-134) submits DAY limit orders at 85% of a 15-min-delayed indicative mid, which routinely rest; broker.get_orders (broker.py:162-165) and broker.cancel (broker.py:159-160) have zero call sites (grep co
fix: At gate time (and before the LLM propose stage), fetch broker.get_orders(status='open') and treat every open order whose client_order_id starts with 'veritas-open-' as one spread: add 2 to the leg-position count toward max_open_positions and add its adjusted_max_loss to the heat numerator — cache {client_order_id: adjusted_max_loss} when open_credit_spread submits (have it return the client_order_id) or recompute from the order's legs. On kill/EOD, first cancel every working veritas-* order via cancel_order_by_id (never replace — mleg replace is 403-disabled) and poll until cancellations confirm, then close positions; otherwise a resting order can fill after the flatten and open an untracked position outside the entry window.

title: Positions are dropped from tracking when a close order is merely ACCEPTED (r.ok), not filled; close rejections or partial fills leave live spreads untracked with no retry, and close qty always assumes the full opening order filled
reason: Reproduced. broker.call returns {'ok': True} whenever the MCP result is not an error (broker.py:66-78) — i.e. the reverse-mleg DAY limit was accepted, not filled — and both manage() (position.py:80-82) and kill_switch_close_all() (position.py:109-110) pop the tag on that basis. Once popped, nothing revisits it: manage() iterates open_spreads (and is itself never called), reconcile is report-only.
fix: Treat close submission as pending, never closed: on r.ok, set open_spreads[tag]['status']='closing' and keep the tag; poll get_order_by_id (or get_all_positions) until the reverse order reports filled / the positions disappear, and only then pop. On timeout or rejection, keep the tag with 'close_failed' and retry on the next manage/kill pass while the option market is open, escalating to alerts if it persists past 16:00 ET. Submit closes with qty = actual broker position qty from get_all_positions (per spread pairing), not spread.contracts, and verify the opening order's filled_qty/filled_avg_price via get_order_by_id before using entry_credit in exit math (replace main.py:91's acceptance-time mark_filled with a fill-verification step). If a close is rejected with 403 'uncovered' (Alpaca already closed the short leg near expiry), close the remaining long leg alone via close_position (single-symbol close is permitted) and flag for manual review.

title: Portfolio-heat numerator is wrong in both directions: only put-leg symbols counted (call spreads contribute zero heat), market_value used as a proxy for max loss, and non-option symbols like assigned 'SPY' shares match the 'P' substring check
reason: Reproduced. main.py:70 counts abs(market_value) only where 'P' in symbol[-9:]. OCC symbols end in the type char at index -9 followed by 8 strike digits, which contain no letters, so call legs ('...C00450000') never match — every bear_call spread contributes zero heat for its whole life. For puts, |market_value| is the current close cost, not max loss: a spread that has decayed toward profit has ti
fix: Add one helper is_option_symbol(sym): asset_class=='us_option' when available, else the OCC type char at symbol[-9] in ('P','C') (note data.py:134's [-8] fallback is off by one — the type char is at [-9]; align all three sites on the helper). Replace main.py:70's numerator with tracked risk: sum(adjusted_max_loss) over open_spreads (tracked + adopted per finding 1) instead of abs(market_value); for untracked broker option positions either adopt them or estimate max loss from OCC strike spacing (width*100*|qty| minus mark) before the gate runs. Equity positions (assigned SPY shares etc.) are excluded from all option logic by the asset_class filter, fixing the false-positive DoS.

title: max_notional_per_spread ($3,000) is defined as a hard limit but never enforced anywhere in the pipeline
reason: Reproduced by grep: max_notional_per_spread appears exactly once in the codebase (config.py:69, inside the 'Risk gates (NOT LLM-overridable)' block); neither validator.validate() nor risk.evaluate() references it, and open_credit_spread takes spread.contracts unchecked. _pick_strikes (candidates.py:39-43, 50-54) snaps the long leg to the nearest listed strike at least 0.5 away from the short, so w
fix: Wire it into risk.evaluate(): gates['notional'] = spread.width * 100 * spread.contracts <= SETTINGS.max_notional_per_spread, with a failure message like the other gates (and optionally a clamp/reject in validator.validate() so it is caught pre-risk). Add a regression test asserting a width-5 x contracts-5 candidate is blocked.

title: EOD force-close gives up after one attempt and then blocks the entire asyncio loop with time.sleep — failed closes are not retried before market close and the reconcile/heartbeat tasks starve
reason: Reproduced. main.py:131-136: on should_force_close() the loop calls kill_switch_close_all once, discards its return value, writes 'eod_done' unconditionally, then executes synchronous time.sleep(max(60, 3600)) — always 3600s — blocking the single-threaded event loop, so the reconcile task (main.py:124) and the MCP session cannot run for an hour. kill_switch_close_all appends per-tag results (posit
fix: Replace time.sleep with await asyncio.sleep (keeps the reconcile task and MCP session alive). After each EOD/kill close pass, inspect kill_switch_close_all's returned results: while any open_spreads tags or broker option positions remain AND the Alpaca clock still shows the option market open (before 16:00 ET), retry failed closes every ~30-60s with await asyncio.sleep, canceling any working veritas orders first; after RTH, stop submitting (orders are rejected) and escalate to loud alerts (audit + stdout + non-zero exit marker / external notifier) listing unclosed symbols for manual intervention. Finally, sleep to the next session using clock.next_open (already captured in data.py's snapshot) instead of a fixed 3600s block. Apply the same inspect-and-retry treatment to the daily-loss kill path at main.py:73-75.

title: --loop has no exception guard around run_cycle; one transient error kills the entire unattended process
reason: Reproduced the core defect from the code: main.py:130-138 runs `await run_cycle(...)` inside `while True` with no try/except (only a bare `finally` at 139 that cancels the reconcile task); any exception propagates through main_loop -> asyncio.run -> process exit. Concrete raisers verified: (1) decision.py:54 uses the sync `Anthropic` client and line 91 `messages.create` has no try/except anywhere
fix: In main_loop, wrap the per-cycle call: `try: await run_cycle(...) except asyncio.CancelledError: raise except Exception as e: _safe_audit(audit, "loop", "cycle_error", error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")` then fall through to the asyncio.sleep. Add a _safe_audit helper (try/except OSError -> stderr) and use it in reconcile_loop's except handler too. Harden decision.py: (a) guard the response — `if not resp.content or not hasattr(resp.content[0], "text"): return TradeProposal(action="NO_TRADE", thesis="empty LLM response")`; (b) wrap messages.create in `except anthropic.APIError` returning a NO_TRADE proposal; (c) pass max_retries to the Anthropic constructor for built-in 429/5xx backoff; (d) wrap `TradeProposal(**data)` in try/except pydantic.ValidationError -> NO_TRADE (no fence-split change needed — the guard at line 100 makes IndexError impossible). Supervise the reconcile task: restructure reconcile_loop so its body can never exit (nest a while-True around the try/except), and have main_loop re-create the task if it observes it done.

title: EOD path: time.sleep(3600) blocks the event loop and the schedule never re-syncs to the next 9:30 open
reason: Confirmed by code reading plus arithmetic: main.py:135 `time.sleep(max(60, 3600))` — max() of two literals is always 3600 (dead constant; the comment 'sleep until next session start' confirms intent), and it executes on the event-loop thread, freezing the reconcile task, asyncio timers, and MCP stdio reads for a full hour (demonstrated: a loop-thread time.sleep delays a concurrent task by the whol
fix: Replace main.py:131-136 with an async, calendar-aware wait: fetch the clock via a small helper (`await asyncio.to_thread(data.trading.get_clock)` or reuse the last snapshot's snap.clock['next_open'], an aware datetime from alpaca-py) and `await asyncio.sleep(max(60, (next_open - now_et).total_seconds() + 60))` — never time.sleep, so the loop stays live and the reconcile task keeps detecting overnight assignments. Gate should_force_close() and in_entry_window() with a market calendar (exchange_calendars XNYS, or at minimum clock.is_open + weekday/holiday check) so weekends/holidays neither spin overnight nor attempt entries during 10:00-15:00 ET (where the wall-clock gate currently passes). Keep the spin-exit condition anchored to the next session start (next_open), not wall-clock wrap-around.

title: open_spreads lives only in memory: after a restart, kill-switch/EOD force-close is a no-op while real positions exist at the broker
reason: Verified from the code: position.py:33 `self.open_spreads: dict[str, dict] = {}` is the sole record; grep shows no persistence (no json.dump/write_text/save in the package) and no rebuild path — main_loop constructs PositionManager with an empty dict and nothing replays broker/audit state into it. Consequences verified: (a) after any restart, kill_switch_close_all (position.py:105-110) iterates an
fix: Persist open_spreads to a JSON file under SETTINGS.data_dir on every register_open/close/pop (atomic tmp+replace write), and rebuild at boot in main_loop after `pm.broker = broker`: load persisted spreads, then `positions = await broker.get_positions()` + `orders = await broker.get_orders(status='open')`; drop entries whose legs no longer exist at the broker and adopt broker-only option positions as unknown spreads (legs built from OCC symbols, qty/side from the position, entry_credit from fill activities via get_account_activities) so kill-switch/EOD can close them — full spreads ONLY via reverse mleg close_credit_spread (close_position is per-symbol and 403s 'uncovered' on spreads); a lone short leg left by pin-risk handling has no spread partner and should go through close_position for that single symbol. Put the close-side idem_tag into the OPEN order's client_order_id (e.g. veritas-open-<tag>-<uuid>) so broker orders map back to tags without needing the execution audit event. Change main.py:91/mark_filled to record status='submitted' and set 'filled' only when reconcile sees both legs in broker positions.

title: Blocking sync SDK calls inside the event loop starve the reconcile task every cycle
reason: Verified: main.py:42 calls `data.capture()` synchronously on the loop; data.py:53-148 makes ~11 sequential sync REST calls (get_clock, get_account, get_all_positions, then per underlier: stock latest quote + daily bars + 5-min bars, plus one option chain each — 2 underliers). main.py:60 calls `brain.decide(...)`, and decision.py:54/91 use the sync Anthropic client whose messages.create blocks 5-60
fix: Minimal change: `snap = await asyncio.to_thread(data.capture)` and `proposal = await asyncio.to_thread(brain.decide, feats, candidates, snap.positions, snap.account, pnl_today)` — keeps reconcile alive through capture+LLM with no API changes. Cleaner long-term: AsyncAnthropic in decision.py and alpaca-py async clients in data.py. Leave AuditLog.write sync for now (small, and its full-sync write is what currently makes interleaving impossible); if it is ever moved to to_thread, serialize with a lock.

title: McpBroker: no timeout on call_tool (subprocess hang stalls the loop forever) and no reconnect after subprocess death
reason: Verified from broker.py: `await self._client.call_tool(tool, args)` at line 65 has no timeout — grep confirms the only asyncio.wait_for in the repo is main.py:102 (stop.wait), so a deadlocked stdio subprocess stalls the awaiting task (main loop during order submission, or reconcile during get_positions) forever, and call()'s retry/backoff never engages. Death path: __aenter__ is invoked exactly on
fix: In call(): `result = await asyncio.wait_for(self._client.call_tool(tool, args), timeout=SETTINGS.mcp_call_timeout)` (add e.g. 60s to config) so a hang surfaces as a transport exception and the existing retry/backoff engages. Add reconnect INSIDE call(): on transport-closed-type errors (or N consecutive 'retries exhausted'), `await self._client.__aexit__(None, None, None)` then re-run the __aenter__ sequence (`self._client = Client(self._params); await self._client.__aenter__()`) and retry with the SAME args dict — the same-args retry is what makes re-submission safe (duplicate client_order_id is rejected 422 across full order history). Do NOT retry at the open_credit_spread level by regenerating the order: that builds a NEW client_order_id and can double-submit if the original reached Alpaca; any higher-level retry must first check get_orders for the existing client_order_id. Expose `async def ensure_connected()` and call it at the top of each run_cycle and reconcile tick.

title: PositionManager.manage() is never called: profit-take, stop-loss, and 0DTE force-close never execute
reason: Verified by grep over the whole repo: `manage(` appears only at its definition (position.py:50); no call sites in main.py, tests, or tools. So the module docstring's exit policy — profit take at 50% of credit, stop at 200%, 0DTE force-close at 15:30, and the 15:45 pin-risk guard inside manage() — is entirely dead code. The only closers are kill_switch_close_all via the daily-loss kill (main.py:73-
fix: Drive manage() from reconcile_loop (inside its existing try/except): add an option-latest-quote helper — data.py already imports OptionLatestQuoteRequest unused, and the MCP server exposes get_option_latest_quote — fetch quotes for the legs of each entry with status=='filled' (per the open_spreads persistence/status fix), compute per-tag buy-back cost = short-leg ask - long-leg bid (manage() indexes mark_prices by tag), and call `actions = await pm.manage(prices_by_tag)` each tick, auditing the actions. This activates profit-take (50% of credit), stop-loss (200%), 0DTE force-close at 15:30, and the 15:45 pin-risk guard. Close attempts remain reverse-mleg via close_credit_spread; rely on reconcile to confirm actual closes since a limit close may itself not fill.

title: Audit log: per-event blocking file open/close in the event loop, and the file date is UTC so ET-evening events roll into the next day's file
reason: Both parts verified. (1) audit.py:21 builds the filename from `utcnow()` (models.py:13 returns timezone.utc), so the file boundary is UTC midnight — 20:00 ET in EDT, 19:00 ET in EST (offset arithmetic verified). The 9:30-16:00 ET RTH session stays within one UTC date as the reviewer concedes, but any ET-evening events — exactly what the current EOD overnight spin and a running reconcile produce be
fix: Derive the file date in ET: in _path() (and read_day's default) use `datetime.now(ZoneInfo(NY_TZ)).strftime('%Y-%m-%d')` so one trading day maps to one file (reuse NY_TZ from config.py); note this requires the tzdata package on Windows, which pyproject.toml does not list — add it. Wrap write()'s open/write in try/except OSError that prints to stderr as a last resort instead of raising into run_cycle or reconcile_loop. A long-lived handle (open once per date, reopen on rollover) is optional; if writes are ever moved into threads, guard the append with an asyncio.Lock or a thread lock.

title: resp.content[0].text crashes on thinking blocks and refusals (stop_reason never checked)
reason: Reproduced from the code: decision.py:91-98 calls messages.create with no output_config and no stop_reason inspection, then unconditionally reads resp.content[0].text. Per verified platform docs: (1) claude-sonnet-5 runs adaptive thinking by default when `thinking` is omitted, so ThinkingBlock objects can appear in content (typically first, since thinking precedes the final text) and they expose `
fix: In decision.py replace lines 98-107 with: branch on stop_reason first — if resp.stop_reason == "refusal": return TradeProposal(action="NO_TRADE", thesis="LLM refused request"); if resp.stop_reason == "max_tokens": return TradeProposal(action="NO_TRADE", thesis="LLM output truncated (max_tokens)"); then text = next((b.text for b in resp.content if getattr(b, "type", None) == "text"), ""). Keep the existing fence-strip + json.loads(text) path unchanged (empty text -> JSONDecodeError -> existing NO_TRADE fallback). Additionally wrap the json.loads/TradeProposal construction in try/except (see finding 2) so the documented 'fail-safe NO_TRADE semantics' actually hold for every LLM-output variant.

title: JSONDecodeError is the only handled failure: non-dict JSON and pydantic ValidationError crash decide() uncaught
reason: Reproduced from the code. decision.py:104 catches only json.JSONDecodeError; decision.py:106-107 do data.pop and TradeProposal(**data) unguarded. (a) json.loads('[1,2]') succeeds and data.pop raises AttributeError — confirmed no isinstance check exists. (b) pydantic v2 lax mode rejects non-integral floats for int fields (1.5 -> ValidationError) and cannot coerce None to int or 'many'/'high' to int
fix: In decision.py: (1) after json.loads, guard the shape: if not isinstance(data, dict): return TradeProposal(action="NO_TRADE", thesis=f"LLM returned non-object JSON: {type(data).__name__}"). (2) Wrap construction in try/except ValidationError (from pydantic import ValidationError) returning TradeProposal(action="NO_TRADE", thesis=f"LLM JSON failed schema validation: {[str(x) for x in e.errors()[:3]]}") — the .pop('spread', None) must happen on the dict before model_validate. Keep TradeProposal(**data) via model_validate with the existing permissive coercions; bounds stay in validator.py. (3) In models.py:86 change confidence to confidence: float = Field(default=0.0, ge=0.0, le=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False). Also add the same to any other float the LLM supplies if custom legs are ever re-enabled. All three paths now return the safe NO_TRADE instead of raising.

title: Structured outputs claimed in config but never sent; JSON extraction relies on a fragile fence heuristic
reason: Confirmed from the code and platform facts. config.py:34-35 comment claims determinism comes from structured outputs 'See decision.py', but decision.py:91-97 passes no output_config — the model gets free text and lines 100-101 apply the fence heuristic. Each breakage reproduces from the string logic: (a) 'Here is my decision:\n```json\n{...}' fails startswith('```') so the fence is never stripped
fix: Add the structured-output call and keep the hardening: resp = self.client.messages.create(model=SETTINGS.llm_model, max_tokens=4096, system=SYSTEM, messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user}], output_config={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "schema": DECISION_SCHEMA}}) where DECISION_SCHEMA uses only supported keywords (types, enum, anyOf, additionalProperties:false — no minimum/maximum), then STILL apply the finding-1 fix verbatim (stop_reason refusal/max_tokens branches, type-selected text block) because json_schema does not cover refusals or truncation, and keep the finding-2 shape/ValidationError guards. json.loads of the text block can then stay; the fence-strip heuristic becomes redundant and can be deleted or kept as dead-code fallback. Numeric bounds remain enforced by pydantic (models.py ge/le) and validator.py exactly as they already are — do not move them into the schema.

title: max_tokens=1024 truncation and refusals degrade into an unlabeled NO_TRADE with no audit event
reason: Reproduced from the code and confirmed against platform docs. decision.py:93 sets max_tokens=1024 and lines 98-105 never read resp.stop_reason. Docs confirm on Sonnet 5 max_tokens is a hard cap on thinking + response text together and that with thinking omitted, adaptive runs — so 1024 can be consumed by reasoning before the JSON, yielding stop_reason='max_tokens' with truncated text. On truncatio
fix: In decision.py: raise max_tokens to 4096 (cheap headroom for a few-hundred-token JSON plus adaptive thinking; think of 1024 as the Sonnet-4.6-era cap that now also pays for thinking). Apply the finding-1 stop_reason branching so 'refusal', 'max_tokens', and 'end_turn' produce distinct NO_TRADE theses. For auditability, the cleanest implementation is to give DecisionCore an optional audit handle (or a callback) and emit an event per non-end_turn outcome: audit.write(cycle, "decision_fallback", stop_reason=resp.stop_reason, model=resp.model, output_tokens=resp.usage.output_tokens, excerpt=text[:200]) — cycle_id() is generated in main.run_cycle, so either pass `cyc` into decide() or emit the fallback event in run_cycle right after decide() by inspecting a marker on the proposal; do NOT leave raw LLM output as the only trace in the thesis field. main.py:61 already logs the final proposal (llm_proposal stage), which combined with a decision_fallback event answers 'why did the agent stop trading today' without any prose-forensics.
